thread:
Maya (Design): dropping a compact variant prototype for the latency card — goal: keep p95 prominent, heatmap usable, and add a single-line control row with sampling toggle, copy/CSV, and timepicker. preview: https://www.figma.com/file/def456/compact-latency-card

Maya (Design): question for the group: is an icon-only sampling control discoverable enough when the card is collapsed? alternatives: icon+badge (e.g., "1/10"), or move sampling into kebab menu.

Kevin (Eng): leaning to icon+badge. icon-only will have accessibility downsides and could be missed visually. implementation note: popover-based slider for presets is easiest for us than inline controls.

Ava (PM): for incident flows, a visible copy-to-clipboard is very valuable. Can we make the copy button visible in compact, but dim it when the card isn't pinned? also want the button to clarify what is copied (visible timeframe vs full series).

Jules (Accessibility): if it's visible, ensure the copy button includes aria-label like "Copy visible timeframe as CSV (up to 10,000 rows)". also keyboard order should be logical: timepicker -> sampling -> copy. focus ring contrast must meet AA.

Maya (Design): good point on focus order. originally I had copy between timepicker and sampling; swapping to match accessibility advice.

Kevin (Eng): technical constraint: compact card width varies across dashboards. If we keep the timepicker left we should collapse the textual date into an icon-only control (calendar icon) with a tooltip showing the range. Avoid moving primary alignment between cards.

Ava (PM): microcopy suggestion: rename "Auto-sample" to "Adaptive sampling" in tooltips and accessibility labels. Users complained "auto" was ambiguous in usability tests.

Maya (Design): adopting "Adaptive sampling". Also adding tooltip on copy button: "Copy visible range as CSV" and an unobtrusive toast for success: "Copied 1 row(s) — visible window".

Jules (Accessibility): toast should be aria-live polite and include the number of rows. Also ensure the sampling toggle supports aria-pressed and has aria-live updates when users change presets (so screen readers hear "Sampling: 1 in 10").

Kevin (Eng): we'll use console-bot to emit toasts and analytics. Also will add a 5s throttle on copy to avoid accidental flood during incident runbooks.

Maya (Design): visual accessibility: heatmap legend buckets currently use hue only. Can we add pattern overlays (dots/stripes) for colorblind folks? also increase contrast between buckets 2 and 3.

Jules (Accessibility): yes — pattern + color is best. For hover tooltips on the p95 point, include aria-describedby pointing to a hidden element with the exact percentile label so screen readers read it consistently.

Kevin (Eng): noted. Implementation plan: icon+badge sampling button -> opens popover with slider + quick presets (1/1, 1/5, 1/10). Copy button triggers navigator.clipboard.writeText(csv) + console-bot toast. Event: compact_clipboard_clicked with sampling_rate property. Throttle client-side 5s.

Maya (Design): I'll update Figma with icon states (default/hover/focus/disabled), the microcopy strings, and the pattern overlays for heatmap legend. Will add an a11y checklist in the spec.

Ava (PM): request: add a small telemetry event when sampling preset is changed (sampling_changed) and tag whether user used compact card vs expanded. low cardinality only.

Kevin (Eng): will add event and make the sampling presets feature-flagged for a gradual rollout.

Maya (Design): thanks — will ping when assets are ready. Jules, want to pair on tooltip/aria text once I push updates?

Jules (Accessibility): happy to do a quick review. Ping me in the thread.

console-bot: Uploaded 2 assets to staging/latency/compact/ (build 2026-03-23T16:05Z)

Maya (Design): end.
